$comment: #7675 IfcComplexProperty walk budget: ONE vector for all three walks, the server data model (apps/server/src/services/data_model/tests.rs), the Rust STEP exporter's property base (rust/export/src/step_log/base_tests.rs) and the browser's store-wide pass (packages/parser/test/complex-property-budget.test.ts). Bounds, markers and charges live in ifc_lite_core::limits; the budget is one per model, complex_property_output_budget(input bytes), spent in file order of the property sets. Each case is one file; every listed entity must read the same sets, through IfcRelDefinesByProperties. A dataLines or entityIds entry may be a run {"repeat": [lines], "from": a, "count": n} or {"from": a, "count": n}: {i} in each line is a, a+1, ... for n rounds, the lines in order each round. A set is pinned by its property count and its values joined with a newline: inline when short, else by UTF-8 length and SHA-256. Every case's value bytes per entity must stay within the model's output budget. Keep a case that cuts under 64 KB, so its budget is the 1 MiB floor in every harness (the Rust ones add a STEP header); a case that pins no cut may be larger. 'cuts', when present, pins the levels and listings the model's budget cut (the TS store's count).

cases.name: walk-budget
cases.$comment: 'Wide' lists one member 1100 times (visit budget), 'Fan' lists itself 3 times (k^8 under the depth cap alone), 'LongFan' does the same with a 10 KB usage name, and Pset_Refs lists 'LongFan' 100 times (byte budget).

cases.name: visit-cut-nested
cases.$comment: #7718 round-2 review finding 1: the visit cap cuts the nested 'N' level (its only member is visit 1025) while bytes remain, and the set repeats it until the byte budget runs out. The exporter charged that level's bare marker and the server and TS did not, so it cut a different listing.

cases.name: shared-set
cases.$comment: #7718 round-2 review finding 2: one set, a 1100-member complex property over a 10 KB value, shared by 200 walls (27 KB). With a budget per extractPsetsFromIds call the TS walk ran out of heap; with the store-wide budget every wall reads the one value.

cases.name: dedup-shared-complex
cases.$comment: #7718 round-3 review finding 1: the shape a de-duplicating optimiser writes. Geometry-less, 60 shared single values, one 20-member complex property listed by each of 3 000 element sets (about 800 KB). Charging every listing as a fresh walk at 4 bytes per input byte cut 1 639 of 3 000; walked once per id with each repeat charged what it keeps, at 16 bytes per input byte, nothing is cut.

cases.name: unnamed-member
cases.$comment: #7718 round-3 review finding 2: a nested member without a Name is read for its value and charged in every walk. 'Mixed' shows its unnamed member as a bare part; 'Anon' lists a 1 KB unnamed value 1 000 times, so it spends the budget and Pset_Later is cut. The server read an unnamed member as no value (16 B), so it kept Pset_Later whole and showed 'Mixed' without 'anon'.

values: (truncated: nested properties over the walk budget)

cases.name: duplicated-set-record
cases.$comment: #7718 round-3 review finding 3: #30 has two identical records. Every walk reads a set id once, at its last record (core's keep-last, #7682), so Pset_Dup is charged once and Pset_Later stays whole. Read at both records, Pset_Dup's two listings are charged twice more and Pset_Later is cut; the server also kept two Pset_Dup sets.
